                                      DAN KACIR’S INITIAL BRIEF


    TO THE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:
    Comes now Dan Kacir, Pro Se Intervener, in the above-styled and numbered docket and
    files this his Initial Brief
    In summary my property is on Link C-2 and I am opposed to any route that uses Link C-2
    for reasons set forth below including, but not limited to as follows.
    Dan Kacir previously submitted testimony and exhibits and respectfully request that the
    administrative Judges consider his testimony and exhibits in their entirety.
    As set forth in the intervenor’s testimony and exhibits, the proposed project would
    negatively affect Intervenor’s family’s property, agricultural projects, income, future plans
    and use for the property and continued use and enjoyment of the land.
    The proposed Link C-2 will cut our land in two and divide the North part from the South
    Part including our water sources for our cattle, conservation and other projects.
    My Grandfather, Father, Myself and my children have worked hard to be good stewards of
    the land and to the extent possible have intentionally left the land natural so that wildlife
    will have habitat to live and survive. I believe the proposed Transmission line will adversely
    change the habitat and environment.
    The transmission lines will not serve the public or landowners along the route and will
1
     negatively affect all landowners along its path without providing them any benefit.
    As Shown by Dan Kacir’s sworn direct testimony, Item 4465 filed via PUC Interchange on
    May 13, 2026 and the FEMA Regulatory Floodways and Flow Zone Map of the affected
    property, Item 5184 filed via PUC Interchange on May 27, 2026 over a mile of the proposed
    Link C-2 will go through the FEMA regulatory floodway and flow zone as it crosses the
    land owned by Jason Billeck and Dan Kacir. This designated area must be reserved in order
    to discharge the base flood waters. It will require multiple towers to cross those properties
    and will likely violate FEMA law as well as a high likelihood of having damaging negative
    consequences on the remaining land owned by Jason Billeck, Dan Kacir and the Kacir
    family. The advocates for the transmission line have not provided any hydrologic and
    hydraulic analysis to prove the project will result in exactly a 0.00 increase in base flood
    elevations.
    Article VI, Clause 2, otherwise known as the Supremacy Clause, is a foundational provision
    in the U.S. Constitution that establishes the U.S. Constitution, federal laws and treaties as
    the supreme law or the land. It dictates that federal law takes precedence over conflicting
    state laws. The regulatory floodways and flood flow zone areas designated by FEMA are
    Federal Law and a state court must not issue any decision that is in conflict with those laws.
    In addition to the above the advocates for the proposed transmission line have not provided
    any adequate study on the environmental impact that will be caused by their transmission
    line crossing our land.
    In conclusion, for the reasons set forth above I oppose any route that uses Link C-2.




                                                                   Respectfully submitted,



                                                                           /s/ Dan Kacir

TO THE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

Comes now Dan Kacir, Pro Se Intervener, in the above-styled and numbered docket and
files this his Initial Brief

In summary my property is on Link C-2 and I am opposed to any route that uses Link C-2
for reasons set forth below including, but not limited to as follows.

Dan Kacir previously submitted testimony and exhibits and respectfully request that the
administrative Judges consider his testimony and exhibits in their entirety.

As set forth in the intervenor’s testimony and exhibits, the proposed project would
negatively affect Intervenor’s family’s property, agricultural projects, income, future plans
and use for the property and continued use and enjoyment of the land.

The proposed Link C-2 will cut our land in two and divide the North part from the South
Part including our water sources for our cattle, conservation and other projects.

My Grandfather, Father, Myself and my children have worked hard to be good stewards of
the land and to the extent possible have intentionally left the land natural so that wildlife
will have habitat to live and survive. I believe the proposed Transmission line will adversely
change the habitat and environment.

The transmission lines will not serve the public or landowners along the route and will

 negatively affect all landowners along its path without providing them any benefit.

As Shown by Dan Kacir’s sworn direct testimony, Item 4465 filed via PUC Interchange on
May 13, 2026 and the FEMA Regulatory Floodways and Flow Zone Map of the affected
property, Item 5184 filed via PUC Interchange on May 27, 2026 over a mile of the proposed
Link C-2 will go through the FEMA regulatory floodway and flow zone as it crosses the
land owned by Jason Billeck and Dan Kacir. This designated area must be reserved in order
to discharge the base flood waters. It will require multiple towers to cross those properties
and will likely violate FEMA law as well as a high likelihood of having damaging negative
consequences on the remaining land owned by Jason Billeck, Dan Kacir and the Kacir
family. The advocates for the transmission line have not provided any hydrologic and
hydraulic analysis to prove the project will result in exactly a 0.00 increase in base flood
elevations.

Article VI, Clause 2, otherwise known as the Supremacy Clause, is a foundational provision
in the U.S. Constitution that establishes the U.S. Constitution, federal laws and treaties as
the supreme law or the land. It dictates that federal law takes precedence over conflicting
state laws. The regulatory floodways and flood flow zone areas designated by FEMA are
Federal Law and a state court must not issue any decision that is in conflict with those laws.
In addition to the above the advocates for the proposed transmission line have not provided
any adequate study on the environmental impact that will be caused by their transmission
line crossing our land.

In conclusion, for the reasons set forth above I oppose any route that uses Link C-2.

Respectfully submitted,

‘UIMSELE IN OPPOSITION OF SEGMENT C-2

Comes now Dan Kacir who files this Direct Testimony opposing segment C-2, Dan Kacir stipulates that
this Direct Testimony can be treated by all parties as if the answers were filed under oath. And is willing

to be called as a witness at any hearings on these matters.

" PERSONAL INFORMATION:

Q. Please state your name and address.

A. My name is Dan Kacir. My mailing address is P.O. Box 1754, Temple Texas 76503.

Q. Are you an intervenor in this proceeding? If so, please explain how.

A. Yes, I am intervened in this proceeding on behalf of myself, Dan Kacir, in PUC Docket
Number 59475, link C-2 as a property owner that is in the path of C-2

Page 1

 Q. Please state your familiarity with the property.

A. My Grandfather, August Kacir purchased the property in 1929 and it has been in our family
ever since. | live on and have spent the majority of my life on this land where we have a well established
cow Calf cattle ranching operation and pecan orchards.

Despite not having received lawful notice, | currently own a deeded 43 percent of this land filed in

the deed records of Bell County, TX instrument number 2012053767 for parcels 57747 and 57748 and am
named to inherit the rest of this land.

My two children have spent an extensive amount of time working with these operations and
preserving this land and are also deeded co-owners of this farm filed in the deed records of Bell

County, TX under instrument numbers 2023016686 and 2023016687. I also manage native

whitetail deer and other native wildlife on this land.

Q. Are you testifying on your own or on behalf of another entity?

A. On my own behalf.

Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?

A. To oppose the C-2 line.

Q. What is your overall concern with the proposed routing across your property?

A. The route of the C-2 section will come into my property from the East straight across to the West

and will cut the property in two which would separate the North end from the south end. The
proposed route would cut across land that we have established native grasses such as native Indian,
switch and gamma grasses and pecan trees. It would require vegetation clearing and create habitat
fragmentation and impact the wildlife corridors.
The water needs for the farm for cattle and all other purposes are provided by a well that is located
on the North side of the proposed c-2 link and is piped to the all other parts of the farm for our
water needs. The proposed link c-2 would likely interfere with our ability to get the water from the
well located on the North side of link c-2 to the land located on the South side of link c-2. The link
c-2 proposed easement is located over some of the recharge area for our well and altering the shape
of the surface and removing the vegetation raises concerns that it will negatively affect our water
well which is necessary for all of the operations of our farm.

There is no existing right of way across our land on the proposed route of link c-2 and it would cut
Page2.

 across our land. We have not disturbed this ground and have always implemented strict no till
policy to our operations due to the land being located in the flood flow zone.

The use of the farm for our operations will be negatively affected and studies indicate that this will
cause a devaluation in inherited value our land by dividing the farm in two. There are also serious
questions of local benefit and public materials indicated the project will serve limited, if any, local

benefit to myself and the other local landowners who will bear the substantial impact of the

proposed c-2

Q. Have you ever testified at the Public Utility Commission of Texas before?

A. No

NOTICE AND PUBLIC MEETINGS

Q. Did you receive a notice in the mail from the applicants last spring about the project

and the June 2025 public meetings?

A. No, I did not receive any notice in the mail from the applicants last spring or at any

other time regarding the project or the June 2025 public meetings.

Q. Did you receive a packet in the mail from the applicants regarding the proposed

transmission line routes ?

A. No. I received no notification whatsoever from the applicants or the PUC about this transmission

line project.

Q. When did you receive that packet in the mail?

A. I did not receive a packet from Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC despite my deed
being lawfully filed in the deed records of Bell County, Tx

Q. Did you receive any notification from the applicants or the PUC about the project?

A. No. I did not receive any notification whatsoever from the applicants (Oncor and

LCRA), the PUC, or any other party about the Bell County East to Big Hill 765-kV

Page 3.

 transmission line project. I had no knowledge of the project until a friend called me

and told me about one of the posted maps in April of 2026. |

Q. Do you know why you did not receive a notice about the June 2025 public meetings?

A. No

Q. When did you first learn about the project?

A. When a friend called me up and told me that there was a high voltage project proposal that cut across

my land.

Q. Once you received your notification, did you attempt to obtain legal representation or advice
from attorneys who specialize in these types of proceedings?

A. Based on not receiving notice I have not had time to secure legal representation or advice from any

law offices that specialize in Public Utility Commission of Texas legal proceedings.

The severely limited timeline and my inability to obtain legal representation has significantly
hampered my ability to understand the project, prepare for the proceedings, and participate

meaningfully.

Public Utility Commission of Texas proceedings are highly technical and complex for average
landowners. While the Applicants, Commission Staff, and other regular participants treat these
cases as routine, affected landowners like myself are trying to protect our property rights, and
family futures while managing jobs, families, and everyday responsibilities.

Because | did not receive any required notice I have had almost no time to review the extensive filings,

learn the rules, evaluate route alternatives, prepare testimony, or organize with others.

Page 4.


 DUE PROCESS AND TIMELINE CONCERNS

Q. Has the constrained timeline resulting from Oncor's and LCRA's failure to notify you
combined with the lack of available legal representation, hampered your ability to effectively
navigate the project and legal procedures as is necessary to exercise your rights of due

process?

A. Yes.

Argument
The proposed link C-2 has a high likelihood of causing substantial damage to property owner

intervener Dan Kacir’s property for reasons stated above

Prayer

For the reasons stated above in his direct testimony, Property owner intervener Dan Kacir Prays the

Court will deny Link C-2 in its entirety.

Respectfully submitted,

Ga, Foon
